0.text: For people with moderate OCD, intrusive thoughts and compulsions can take up 1 to 3 hours a day, while in the severe form, these can take up more than 8 hours a day.
0.fact: Research shows that more than 60% of people with OCD experience intrusive thoughts daily.

1.text: About 50% of people with OCD report that their intrusive thoughts and compulsions significantly interfere with daily life, including work, school, and social interactions.
1.fact: Frequent and prolonged intrusive thoughts can lead to exhaustion and health issues, such as headaches, digestive problems, and chronic fatigue.

2.text: The intense anxiety caused by intrusive thoughts can manifest as physical symptoms, such as headaches, muscle tension, and digestive issues.
2.fact: Although Franklin D. Roosevelt was not officially diagnosed with OCD, historians note that his intrusive thoughts caused him significant anxiety, which affected his mood and daily life.

3.text: The intensity and frequency of intrusive thoughts can vary greatly from person to person. Some are able to cope with them most of the time, while others experience ongoing difficulty.
3.fact: CBT, especially Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), is the most effective treatment for OCD, helping people learn to resist intrusive thoughts.

4.text: Only about 10–20% of people with OCD report that they can mostly control their intrusive thoughts.
4.fact: Antidepressants, such as SSRIs, often help people with OCD reduce the intensity of intrusive thoughts and improve their ability to manage them.

5.text: Common compulsive actions include frequent hand washing, repeatedly checking locks and appliances, and repetitive behaviors like touching certain objects or repeating specific words and phrases.
5.fact: Fewer than 5% of people with OCD perform compulsive actions for more than 8 hours a day, which seriously interferes with their daily life.

6.text: Compulsive actions can interfere with professional life, reducing productivity and making it difficult to perform work duties. Some people may need to reduce their working hours or even change jobs due to their condition.
6.fact: Howard Hughes' compulsive actions, such as constant hand washing and avoiding contact with others, led to social isolation and significant life changes. Ultimately, his OCD seriously impacted his health and career.

7.text: Compulsive actions are often accompanied by strong negative emotions, such as anxiety, guilt, shame, and frustration. These emotions can significantly increase overall discomfort and feelings of being overwhelmed.
7.fact: People with OCD often experience comorbid conditions, such as depression and anxiety disorders, which can exacerbate their symptoms and increase discomfort.

8.text: Stress and anxiety levels play a significant role in the ability to resist rituals. During periods of increased stress, resisting rituals can become more difficult.
8.fact: Footballer David Beckham has admitted that he sometimes manages to resist performing rituals, especially with the support of his family and therapists.

9.text: Roughly 30–35% of people report that they can control their rituals most of the time.
9.fact: Mindfulness and meditation practices can help improve control over rituals by reducing anxiety and supporting overall mental well-being.

normal.text: Your results indicate an absence of significant signs of obsessive-compulsive disorder. If intrusive thoughts or impulses occur, they don't cause noticeable discomfort or interfere with your daily life. Overall, you're able to maintain control over your thoughts and behavior and feel stable.
normal.title: Normal

light.text: You may occasionally experience repetitive thoughts or the urge to recheck something, especially in stressful situations. These occurrences aren't constant and usually don't disrupt your daily rhythm. You manage to maintain control over these impulses and adapt to daily tasks. If certain thoughts or actions begin to cause anxiety, gentle self-regulation techniques can help maintain your emotional balance.
light.title: Mild OCD symptoms

severe.text: You may encounter persistent thoughts or rituals that help reduce anxiety but sometimes limit your freedom of behavior or take up a noticeable amount of time. The drive for order, control, or specific rituals can create tension, especially if circumstances make it hard to follow your usual rules. You may manage this on your own sometimes, but periodic professional support can be helpful in reducing the burden and increasing your flexibility.
severe.title: Moderate OCD symptoms

extreme.text: Your answers may suggest that intrusive thoughts and rituals significantly affect your daily life and emotional state. You may feel intense anxiety if you're unable to perform certain actions, which can cause significant stress. In such cases, seeking professional help can be an important step toward improving your well-being and reducing tension. Support is available, and you can reach out for it.
extreme.title: Significant OCD signs

text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is associated with intrusive thoughts and repetitive actions that a person performs to reduce anxiety.
OCD symptoms can vary: from occasional intrusive thoughts to repetitive actions and mental rituals that require time and attention.
This condition is quite common, and an important step is to be mindful of your experiences and seek support when needed—this helps maintain your quality of life and mental well-being.
